anchors.why: Kiro's hooks keep reporting working through a tool approval, so its key-bound menu is the only authority, and a pasted Enter answers it. The menu owns the bottom of the screen: choice rows above an `esc to close` key row that ends the output, because an answered menu stays in scrollback. Keyed on the rare `always allow` choice so retained history rarely wakes the blocked scan.

test.regex: ^\s*(?:[>❯›]\s*)?(?:allow|always allow|deny|always deny|yes, single permission|trust, always allow in this session|no \(tab to edit\))$

anchors.why: Kiro's wider approval offers trusting the entire tool, under the same `esc to close` key row that must end the output.
Editing a pending tool call keeps the approval open under a `requires approval · modify request` header, with the edited request on a `>` row, until `esc to close` ends the output.
With subagents running, Kiro gathers their tool approvals into one panel that waits for a choice while its hooks still report working.
